newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTS-Australian wheat exports to China steady.
newsitem.headline: RTS-Australian wheat exports to China steady.

text.p: Australia expects to maintain wheat exports to China of 2.2 million tonnes in the 1996/97 financial year, unchanged from 1995/96, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Wednesday.
The exports would remain steady despite a strong domestic wheat crop in Australia, Australian Wheat Board Chairman Trevor Flugge told a press briefing.

The AWB announced earlier on Wednesday that it and construction firm Transfield Holdings Pty Ltd have together won a A$10 million contract to build a grain terminal at Fang Cheng in Guangxi province, southwest China.
The contract was central to a World Bank Finance Chinese grain handling system modernisation programme valued at A$1.25 billion, Flugge said.
The contract puts the AWB-led consortium in a good position to win a second contract worth A$253 million to construct handling facilities at the northern China port of Dalian in Liaoning province.

The AWB has forecast an Australia wheat crop of 20 million tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March), which would be Australia's second largest on record behind the 1983/84 crop of 22 million tonnes. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
